history.summary: GENERIC NAME - BEST-SUPPORTED REFERENT: the CSV name 'Radhakrishna Temple, Kota' is generic and matches several small shrines (e.g. Shree Radhakrishna Mandir at Pratap Nagar/Borkhera, Radha Krishan Mandir at Kansuwa, Talwandi's Radha Krishna Mandir), but the best-supported and most prominent Radha-Krishna temple in Kota is the SHREE MATHURADEESH JI TEMPLE near Patanpole, Kishorpura, Kota (324001) - documented here as the referent, with the generic CSV name retained in alternate_names. Mathuradheesh ('Lord of Mathura') is a major Vallabhacharya/Pushtimarg (Shuddhadvait) Krishna shrine: the idol of Radha stands beside Krishna in the sanctum. Sources credit its construction to the 17th century under Hada Rajput rule, with Maharao Bhim Singh I (r. 1707-1720) promoting Vaishnavism in the region (placeapp.in - treat the 17th-century dating as weakly sourced, verify). TripAdvisor reviewers describe it as a very old, peaceful Krishna temple popular with families and wish-seekers. COORDINATE FLAG: geocoding 'Mathuradheesh Ji Temple, Patanpole, Kota' resolves to the Shuddhadvait Pratham Peeth, Patan Road, Kaithunipole, Kota 324006 (25.17803, 75.83448) - consistent with the Patanpole vicinity per listings (Near Patanpole, Kishorpura, Kota-324001 per Justdial), but verify the pin on the ground; there is also a separate smaller 'Chote Mathuradhish Ji Ka Mandir' at Rampura near Patanpole.

town_description: Kota, on the Chambal river, is Rajasthan's education hub and a historic Hada Rajput principality. The Mathuradheesh temple stands near Patanpole in the Kishorpura area, close to the Chambal riverfront (Kaithunipole/Bhatt Ji Ghat side), in the old-city temple belt around Rampura and Kishorpura.
